scores.evidence: Phase 1 MVP: "Ingestion, hybrid retrieval, rerank, grounded answers with citations, basic guardrails, eval harness."
scores.rationale: Roughly sensible flow (discovery → ingestion → retrieval → beta → actions), but phases bundle many layers at once and don't prove dependencies before building on them.

scores.evidence: Phase 1 MVP (internal): "Support agents test it as an assistant"
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is discovery only, and the first build is a full-feature internal MVP, not a thin production end-to-end slice.

scores.evidence: "use one embedding model throughout and store the model version with each vector. Re-embed everything whenever the model changes."
scores.rationale: Some choices are stated with defaults (chunk size, embedding), and open questions are listed, but there is no explicit irreversible-decision list with flip conditions.
Nothing addresses ordering of work by blast radius within phases.
Guardrails, PII redaction and visibility filtering are detailed, but security is a standalone section with review only at phases 1–2, not threaded in every phase (Phase 0 and 3 have none).

scores.evidence: "Observability: trace each conversation turn (rewritten query, retrieved IDs and scores, prompt version, model, latency, tokens, cost)."
scores.rationale: Good tracing detail, but it is in a standalone Operations section; the phase table shows dashboards only in Phase 2, not from day zero.

scores.evidence: "prompts, chunking settings, and model choices live in config with version IDs, so you can A/B test and roll back."
scores.rationale: Versioned config, embedding version storage and CI regression gate exist, but no reproducible environments or builds, and not tied to each phase.

scores.evidence: "Availability: if the LLM fails, show plain search results and offer escalation."
scores.rationale: Fallbacks and escalation exist (LLM failure, low confidence, off-hours), but mostly in standalone sections and not phase by phase.

scores.evidence: "If the top rerank score falls below a calibrated threshold, skip generation and go to the clarify-or-escalate path."
scores.rationale: Defenses, human escalation and cost controls are strong, but the roadmap builds retrieval and generation together with only 'basic guardrails'; budgets are weak and the defenses-first ordering isn't explicit.

scores.evidence: "Later, optional: resolved tickets, mined into an FAQ that a human reviews."
scores.rationale: Deferred items (personalization, multilingual, actions, ticket mining) are mentioned and placed in later phases, but without explicit pull-forward conditions.

note: Competent, detailed RAG design with good guardrails, escalation and evaluation, but it is organized as a feature roadmap. It has no production walking skeleton, no decision gates with flip conditions, and security, observability and resilience are not threaded through each phase.
